analysis:
Examined the head text of ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1-1175) and the ProviderLoopConfig.swift patch and base. The changes are state-only: ProviderLoopConfig.swift adds an optional `autopilotPendingCandidates: AutopilotStartInventory.Pending?`, defaulted to nil, and passes it through the init. ProviderLoop.swift (lines 343-404 in head) adds Autopilot state: the autopilotHistory tuple gains a `detail` field, plus adopted-model IDs, holds, download settings and storage reports, a download prefetch coordinator, inventory-awaiting-registration, a cache sweep, background candidate verification, a registration test seam and a transition watchdog. All of this is in-memory declarations with no logic visible here. The init (lines 852-856) filters autopilotInventory to entries that have a non-empty weightHash, are CBv2-supported and are runtime-eligible. That is unchanged by this PR and fails closed. The advertised set is still built only from config.models, with eligibility and GLM checks (lines 873-890), so Autopilot inventory is kept separate from ordinary serving permission. The cache, attestation, App Attest and WebSocket code paths are not touched in the supplied hunks, and the T-041 posture is unchanged. No new network, file, key or auth surface is visible in these units.

The behavior that matters lives in companion files not supplied: ProviderLoop+AutopilotDownload, +AutopilotPlacement and AutopilotStartInventory. The next pass should check three things. First, whether background-verified candidates (`autopilotCandidateVerification`) compute and bind weight hashes before any model joins the Autopilot set or is registered with the coordinator (T-012, T-027). Second, whether the download coordinator verifies artifacts, with no TOCTOU between hash and load. Third, whether adopted models (`autopilotAdoptedModelIDs`) cannot bypass the advertised-set guard in ensureModelLoaded. This pass reached no conclusion on any of these.
